items.what: How strong each Perrigo tie is
items.was: The 26 medicine ties sat in a folded list, each stamped, with no summary of the records they rest on.
items.now: A new table groups them so the scale stays short: the medicines named on both DailyMed labels and Drugs@FDA in one row, and the January 2022 Aller-Fex recall, from FDA recall reports, in another. All are Documented, and each tie is still listed one by one below.
items.why: With 26 ties, one row each would have repeated the same step and records two dozen times; grouping shows at a glance that every Perrigo tie stands on FDA records.

items.what: How the Perrigo page says the company is tied to Kirkland
items.was: The page led with one record, Perrigo packaging Kirkland Aller-Fex in a 2022 recall, and said “Only the Aller-Fex recall names Perrigo so far.”
items.now: The page leads with FDA’s own files, which tie Perrigo to 25 Kirkland Signature medicines; for 13 of them a Perrigo company holds the approval number printed on the Kirkland label. A table lists each one with its FDA number, and the Aller-Fex recall is the first of them.
items.why: Our Nov 5 read of Kirkland labels on DailyMed, checked against Drugs@FDA, added the other ties to our records and to the medicine page, but this page’s wording wasn’t rewritten, so it contradicted its own list of answers for three days.

items.what: What MISA’s label approvals prove, on the MISA Imports page
items.was: Confirmed, by the page’s scale, meant the company or Costco saying so in its own words. MISA files its own label approvals with TTB, so those could read as Confirmed.
items.now: A TTB label approval is a public record naming MISA as importer: Documented, by the rules on How we know. Confirmed would need a code on the bottle that leads to a factory, and the tequila’s NOM number leads to the distillery, not to MISA.
items.why: An importer’s own filing is easy to mistake for the importer vouching for the maker. The scale’s old wording invited that reading, which our stamp rules don’t allow.

items.what: How the Kimberly-Clark page explains the strength of each tie
items.was: Its strength scale put Confirmed at the company or Costco saying so in its own words, which read as if a statement from Kimberly-Clark would lift the facial tissue tie above the FSC code on the box.
items.now: It now follows How we know: Confirmed needs a code on the product that leads to a factory. The FSC code leads to Kimberly-Clark’s certificate, not a mill, so the tissue stays Documented and the diapers stay Reported. No stamp changed.
items.why: The scale was written for the four company pages published that day and didn’t follow our published stamp rules; on this page it muddied why a certificate code on the box isn’t a factory.

items.what: The “Next check” date on the company pages
items.was: Every company page said “Next check Nov 9”. Next week it would have said Nov 16, and so on, but no job was reading the registers and recalls behind these pages; the last read was Nov 3.
items.now: A job on our server re-reads North Dakota’s pet food register and FDA’s recall records for every company each month. Each page shows the date of that next read, Dec 3, or sooner where one of its answers falls due first, as on the Perrigo page.
items.why: Our schedule assumed a weekly script would run the re-read, and kept promising next Monday for it, but no script was set up to run it.

items.now: The page says LNK makes eight Kirkland medicines, among them pain relievers, low-dose aspirin, a sleep aid and an allergy tablet. Some labels print “Manufactured by: LNK International, Inc.”; on others the label file lists LNK as the manufacturing establishment. The recall is one record among them.
items.why: The label files we read on Nov 5 name LNK on seven more Kirkland medicines. They reached our records but not this page’s wording.
